question: Samsung R&D Institute (SRI-B) software engineer, technical round. Reported C++ OOP questions: **What is polymorphism in C++ and what are its types? How do you achieve runtime polymorphism (write the code with a real-life example)? What is an abstract class and a pure virtual function? What are early (static) and late (dynamic) binding? What are virtual functions and friend functions?** The interviewer asked the candidate to reuse the same code to explain binding.
lookingFor: Correct distinction between compile-time and runtime polymorphism.
A clean working example with virtual functions, override and a virtual destructor.
Understanding of how late binding works (vtable) and when early binding applies.
Precise definitions: abstract class, pure virtual, friend.
Ability to explain through code rather than recitation.
followUps: Why must the base class destructor be virtual?
What is object slicing and how does it break polymorphism?
Can a pure virtual function have a body?
Overloading vs overriding vs hiding: what is the difference?
How do virtual functions behave with multiple inheritance?
